items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: The first one was McCoy Tyner and Chick Corea, and I had heard Bill Evans and so those were specifically the influences that catapulted me to try to play piano.

ctx.x: Did you do that out of necessity?

Both necessity and desire. Necessity because I was on the road playing with some musicians that were truly terrible, and sometimes I would just tell them give me my first note or an introductory chord and sort of say lay out. Maybe the bass player knew the tune. And so the other reason was that I wanted to play with the best of musicians and I had to learn their language in order to keep up with them, and the dissatisfaction with the way that some people played, as opposed to the way that I wanted to hear it. And…
